opponent.description: The named opponent to research. The lawful-use case for the L2 residency lookup on this named person has been confirmed.

full_name.description: The opponent's full name. Used for source discovery via WebSearch, to confirm a fetched page is about this person, and as the registration name to match in the L2 residency query.

website_url.description: Optional hint: the opponent's campaign website. When present, fetch directly; when null/absent, discover via WebSearch.

social_urls.description: Optional hints: the opponent's public social-media profile URLs.

is_incumbent.description: true if known to be the incumbent, false if known not to be, null if unknown.

race_context.description: The race the opponent is running in, hydrated by gp-api before dispatch. Disambiguates the right person/page during discovery (same office, jurisdiction, cycle).

state.description: 2-letter state code (e.g. NC). The broker injects this as the WHERE on the L2 residency query.

city.description: City / jurisdiction name, or null. The broker injects this as a WHERE clause on the L2 residency query when present.

election_date.description: The election date for this race, or null. Confirms the right cycle during discovery.

candidate_platform.description: The candidate's own platform / positions, for context only. Used to frame which contrasts matter; the agent does NOT research the candidate here, only the opponent. Sourced from the candidate's website (the Pro-upgrade profile capture). Any field may be null when unwritten.

issues.description: The issues the candidate is running on.

residency_data.description: Whether the L2 residency query returned a matching registration for the named opponent. 'available' when a row matched and a residency finding was produced; 'unavailable' when no row matched (no residency finding emitted, never fabricated). The broker's data-required gate is carved out for 'unavailable' so a web-only result can still publish.

findings.description: One entry per verified vulnerability in the opponent's public record. A finding is emitted ONLY when its source_extract literally appears on the fetched source_url (or, for a residency finding, when an L2 registration row matched). Findings that fail verification are dropped, never invented. The array may be empty.

claim.description: The vulnerability stated plainly: what the candidate could draw a contrast on, grounded in the opponent's own public conduct.

source_url.description: For web findings: the page actually fetched (the broker's returned X-Source-URL after any redirect), matching ^https?://. For a residency finding sourced from L2 (not a fetchable URL), a stable dataset reference (e.g. 'l2:int__l2_nationwide_uniform_w_haystaq').

source_extract.description: For web findings: a verbatim passage from the fetched page that substantiates the claim (verified via verify_quote). For a residency finding: the matched registration fields rendered as text (e.g. registration state/date).

category.description: Which vulnerability category this finding belongs to.

source_title.description: Optional human-readable title of the source page.

occurred_at.description: Optional date the underlying event occurred (not the retrieval date), or null when undated.
